name: screepsmod-auth
description: Contract of the screepsmod-auth mod on a community server (stock screeps/backend-local): password sign-in and registration without reCAPTCHA or e-mail confirmation, password changes, persistent API tokens with optional restrictions and rate limits, Steam/GitHub sign-in when configured, and its own availability checks. Its middleware and routes are registered before backend-local's own routes and server-password check.

provides.authSignin: Stock backend-local has no password sign-in; screepsmod-auth adds it, issuing backend-local session tokens.
provides.registerSubmit: Stock backend-local registers players only through Steam; screepsmod-auth adds password registration.
provides.userName: screepsmod-auth serves the restricted-token username lookup for its API tokens.
provides.userPasswordSet: screepsmod-auth adds password changes (its `/authmod/password/` page and the official account page use it).
provides.userAuthTokenList: screepsmod-auth stores persistent API tokens and lists them like the official account page expects.
provides.userAuthTokenCreate: screepsmod-auth creates persistent API tokens (full or restricted to endpoints, socket channels and memory segments).
provides.authQueryToken: screepsmod-auth reports the permissions of a persistent API token, as node-screeps-api queries before choosing its user lookup.
provides.userNoRateLimit: screepsmod-auth lifts its rate limits for one API token for two hours.
provides.authSteam: screepsmod-auth adds Steam OpenID sign-in (and account linking) in a browser popup when the server has a Steam Web API key.
provides.authGithub: screepsmod-auth adds GitHub OAuth sign-in (and account linking) in a browser popup when the server has GitHub OAuth credentials.
provides.userUnlinkSteam: screepsmod-auth removes a linked Steam identity.
provides.userUnlinkGithub: screepsmod-auth removes a linked GitHub identity.

adaptations.authSignin: Failed credentials answer HTTP 401 with the plain text `Unauthorized`, banned accounts HTTP 403 `{error: "banned"}`, and HTTP Basic credentials are accepted instead of the JSON body (override: path, Basic security scheme).
adaptations.registerSubmit: Only `username` and `password` are needed; no field is validated and a missing `username` fails with an HTTP 500 HTML error page (override: path).
adaptations.userName: An account without a username answers HTTP 404 `{error: "User not found"}` (override: path).
adaptations.userPasswordSet: `oldPassword` is required only when the account already has a password (override: path).
adaptations.userAuthTokenCreate: An invalid `description` or `memorySegments` answers HTTP 400 with `{ok: 0, error}` (override: path).
adaptations.authQueryToken: The reply nests the whole token record, including its `_id`, under `token`, lists endpoints and socket groups in the mod's own notation, and unknown tokens answer HTTP 200 `{error: "token not found"}` (override: AuthQueryTokenResponse).
adaptations.userNoRateLimit: Requires a signed-in session instead of a reCAPTCHA response; an unknown token prefix answers HTTP 404 `{ok: 0}` and a failed exemption HTTP 400 `{ok: 0}` (override: path).
adaptations.registerCheckUsername: screepsmod-auth answers the check before backend-local: a taken name is `User Exists` (exact, case-sensitive match), never `exists` or `invalid username`, and no server password is checked (override: path).
adaptations.registerCheckEmail: screepsmod-auth answers the check before backend-local: a ban-marked address is `banned: <fields>`, a taken one `User Exists` (exact match), never `exists` or `invalid email`, and no server password is checked (override: path).
adaptations.userCodeSet: screepsmod-auth also accepts HTTP Basic credentials for code uploads and rejects banned accounts with HTTP 403 `{error: "banned"}` (override: path, Basic security scheme).

additions.authModInfo: node-screeps-api calls `GET /api/authmod` on unofficial servers to identify the authentication mod and whether password registration is open.

behaviour.summary: Every request carrying a valid backend-local session token in `X-Token` (on any route, before routing) receives a fresh session token in the `X-Token` and `X-Username` response headers; authenticated backend-local routes then issue another. Session tokens are 40 hex characters (HMAC-SHA1), valid for 60 s after issue; persistent API tokens are never rotated.

Before routing, a token sent as `X-Token` or as the `_token` query parameter is copied into `X-Token` and `X-Username`, so backend-local's token authentication no longer needs `X-Username`. Wherever backend-local authenticates, persistent API tokens (UUIDs created by `userAuthTokenCreate`) are accepted alongside session tokens. A restricted token may call only its listed endpoints (others answer HTTP 403 `{error: "forbidden"}`), only the memory segments it lists, and subscribe only to its console, memory and room socket channels.

An authenticated request (valid `X-Token` session token, or HTTP Basic credentials on `POST /api/user/code`) passes backend-local's server-password check without `X-Server-Password`. The mod's own routes are registered before that check and never require the server password, but password registration is disabled while `SERVER_PASSWORD` is set.

With `rateLimitEnabled` (off by default), requests authenticated by a persistent API token are counted per token: a global bucket (120 per minute) and per-endpoint buckets of the official limits. Each counted reply carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix seconds); an exhausted bucket answers HTTP 429 `text/plain` `Rate limit exceeded, retry after <ms>ms`. Session-token requests and the token-management routes are never limited.

Serves the static password-change page under `/authmod/` (`/authmod/password/`) and registers the server features `auth` (version 1), `auth-tokens` (no version) and `screepsmod-auth` (its package version, `authTypes`, Change Password menu entry); stock backend-local publishes no features, screepsmod-admin-utils lists them in `GET /api/version`.

notes.authSignin: `email` is matched exactly against stored usernames and e-mail addresses (case-sensitive), so a username signs in too; `recaptcha` and `steamTicket` are ignored. Passwords are verified as PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes; accounts without a password (Steam or GitHub sign-ups) cannot sign in. Success is `{ok: 1, token}` with a 40-hex backend-local session token valid for 60 s.
notes.registerSubmit: Stores the account as submitted: no username, e-mail or password rules, no reCAPTCHA, no e-mail confirmation and no token (sign in afterwards). The account gets the configured `registerCpu` (100 by default), is blocked when `preventSpawning` is set, and gets a `default` branch from `modules` (default `{main: ""}`) and empty Memory. Existing username (exact match) or e-mail: `{error}` holding the whole error stack, beginning `Error: User already exists`; a ban-marked e-mail: `banned: <fields>`; while `SERVER_PASSWORD` is set: `Registration is automatically disabled. A server password has been set.` `recaptcha`, `tutorialDone` and `branches` are ignored.
notes.userName: Accepts session tokens and persistent API tokens (including restricted tokens that list `GET /api/user/name`).
notes.userPasswordSet: A missing `password` answers `{ok: 0, error: "Password required"}`; the new password is stored as a PBKDF2-SHA256 hash without length or strength rules. Defect of the mod: when the account has a password and `oldPassword` is wrong, it answers HTTP 401 `{error: "Unauthorized"}` but then still overwrites the stored password and salt with undefined values (the account can no longer sign in with a password) and replies a second time, which throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` and crashes the backend process. Never send a wrong `oldPassword` to a screepsmod-auth server.
notes.userAuthTokenList: Lists every persistent token of the account with `token` masked to its first 8 characters (`xxxxxxxx-****-****-****-************`), `full`, `description` (`null` when none), for restricted tokens `endpoints` (`/api/game/` shortened to `/api/`), `websockets` (`console`, `rooms`) and `memorySegments` (strings), and `noRatelimitUntil` only while an exemption lasts.
notes.userAuthTokenCreate: `type: "selected"` creates a restricted token, any other value a full one. Restricted tokens keep only the endpoints the mod supports (`GET /api/user/name`, `GET /api/user/money-history`, `GET`/`POST /api/user/memory`, `GET`/`POST /api/user/memory-segment`, `GET /api/game/market/orders-index`, `orders`, `my-orders`, `stats`; the official client's `/api/market/...` keys are accepted), `websockets.console`/`rooms`, and `memorySegments` as ids 0-99 separated by commas or spaces (blank = all). The reply's `token` is a UUID.
notes.userAuthTokenDelete: Deletes the caller's token whose `_id` is `tokenId`; succeeds with `{ok: 1}` even when no token matched.
notes.authQueryToken: Unauthenticated. Looks the token up by its full value.
notes.userNoRateLimit: `token` is a prefix of one of the caller's tokens; the matching token is meant to be exempt from rate limits for two hours. Observed on screeps 4.3.0 with the default storage: a matching prefix answered HTTP 400 `{ok: 0}` and the exemption was not applied.
notes.authSteam: Requires the server's Steam Web API key (`STEAM_KEY`). The popup's final page posts `{username, token, steamid}` (a session token) to the opener; a `token` query parameter (stored in a cookie) links the Steam identity to that account, otherwise an account is found or created (100 CPU, `default` branch). Ban-marked identities get an HTTP 403 page posting `{error: "banned: ..."}`.
notes.authGithub: Without `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` every request answers HTTP 503 `GitHub OAuth is not configured.`. Otherwise the popup's final page posts `{username, token}` to the opener, linking to the account of a `token` query parameter or finding/creating an account; `repoScope` is ignored.
notes.registerCheckEmail: Looks up `email` exactly as given; storage errors answer `{error: <message>}`.
notes.userCodeSet: With an `Authorization: Basic` header (username or e-mail and password) and no `X-Token`, the mod authenticates the upload itself and passes it to backend-local with a fresh session token.

requestBody.description: JSON credentials; may be omitted when HTTP Basic credentials are sent.

401.description: Missing or wrong credentials: the authentication middleware ends the response with the text `Unauthorized` and no `Content-Type` header.

username.description: Stored as given (and lower-cased as `usernameLower`); no format rule.

email.description: Optional; stored as given, no format rule.

password.description: Stored as a PBKDF2-SHA256 hash; no length rule.

500.description: A missing or non-string `username` throws before the handler's error envelope; Express answers with its HTML error page.

404.description: The account has no username: `{error: "User not found"}`.

oldPassword.description: Current password; checked only when the account already has a password.

token.description: Prefix of one of the caller's API tokens (the account page sends its first 8 characters).

400.description: The exemption failed: `{ok: 0, error}`, `error` absent when the storage error has no message.

404.description: No token of the caller starts with `token`: `{ok: 0}`.

200.description: `{ok: 1}` when no account has exactly this username, otherwise `{error: "User Exists"}` (HTTP 200).

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: E-mail address to look up (exact match).

200.description: `{ok: 1}` when the address is free; otherwise HTTP 200 `{error}`: `banned: <fields>` for a ban-marked address, `User Exists` when an account has exactly this address.

get.description: Reports screepsmod-auth and the sign-in methods it offers: `name`, `version` (package version), `allowRegistration` (false while `SERVER_PASSWORD` is set), `steam` (always true), `github` and `gitlab` (true when their OAuth credentials are configured).

AuthQueryTokenResponse.x-plugin-reason: screepsmod-auth nests the token record, including its `_id`, under `token` instead of sending `_id` beside it.

AuthQueryTokenResult.x-plugin-reason: screepsmod-auth returns its stored token record: `_id`, the full `token`, `description` `null` when none, socket groups `console`/`rooms`, memory segment ids as strings and an active rate-limit exemption.

description.description: Description given at creation; `null` when none.

endpoints.description: Restricted tokens only: permitted endpoints as `METHOD /api/path`, with `/api/game/` shortened to `/api/`.

websockets.description: Restricted tokens only: permitted socket channel groups.

memorySegments.description: Restricted tokens only, when limited: permitted memory segment ids.

noRatelimitUntil.description: Unix milliseconds until which the token is exempt from rate limits; present only while the exemption lasts.

Basic.description: HTTP Basic credentials (username or e-mail address, password) checked by screepsmod-auth; accepted by `POST /api/auth/signin` and `POST /api/user/code`.
Basic.x-plugin-reason: screepsmod-auth authenticates these routes with HTTP Basic credentials as well.

Token.description: Backend-local session token (40 hex characters from `authSignin`, Steam or GitHub sign-in; valid for 60 s and replaced in the `X-Token` response header of every request that carries it) or a persistent screepsmod-auth API token (a UUID from `userAuthTokenCreate`; never rotated, optionally restricted and rate limited). Also accepted as the `_token` query parameter. Never send tokens to untrusted hosts or follow authenticated cross-host redirects.
Token.x-plugin-reason: screepsmod-auth rotates session tokens on every request and accepts its persistent API tokens wherever session tokens are accepted.

LegacyUsername.description: Legacy header: the official web client sends the token value here as well as in X-Token. Optional: screepsmod-auth copies `X-Token` (or `_token`) into it before backend-local authenticates.
LegacyUsername.x-plugin-reason: screepsmod-auth fills `X-Username` from the token, so backend-local no longer needs it.
